critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the neighbour_shuffle twin gives the same gain per covered pair (after reweighting its 10x lower coverage), the category-entry lift carries no signal.

critiques.text: No leak found. Views are in [t-14d, t) and the co-view graph is built from all sessions in [t-3d, t). active_users only selects the seed users, and the <=5-product filter is per user. Top-6 neighbours break ties by pb. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: difference of differences: compare the gain on low-activity users (<=5 viewed products) with the same feature on users above 5; if the gains match, the stratum claim is refuted.

critiques.text: No leak found. Session first-view times are in [t-7d, t). Seeds come from active users' views in [t-48h, t). The top-25 neighbours break ties by hash(a, b). The twin permutes ft within a session ordered by hash and reads nothing extra. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the time_shuffle twin (which keeps co-occurrence but scrambles order) gives the same gain, directionality carries nothing.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level and reads [t-16d, t) of hist only. Acquisitions fcp < t, and prior-48h views come strictly before the acquisition day. No active_users dependence. The twin's user permutation is ordered by hash.
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compute at t-24h; if the gain is unchanged, the 'retargeted acquisition' lift is only a stable item trait (rival: i_cat_multi_buy_14d, R2 0.764).

critiques.text: No leak found. User events are in [t-14d, t) for active users only, and values are per user. prod uses global carts in [t-7d, t) with ties broken by product_id. The twin's permutations are ordered by hash within the user. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: key level: replace the pair key by the user-category key (drop the product join); if the gain is the same, the feature is only a category-interest proxy.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level and reads [t-7d, t). The landing view is ordered by event_time, then hash(product_id), so it is deterministic. Nothing depends on active_users.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: the twin is already rho 0.90/0.95 with the card. If adding the twin alone recovers the gain, landing position is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level, and d runs from 1 to 7 days before the midnight anchor, so the anchor day is excluded. The global per-day denominators come from the same past window. The twin permutes days by hash(product_id, d).
critiques.kill_test: staleness: the same query at t-24h; if the slope keeps its gain, it does not capture current momentum.

critiques.text: No time or batch leak found. The censoring n.d + lag < t is correct, and active_users only selects ub and ul. However, the card is INVALID: the CTE alias 'glob' is a forbidden word, and the machine test is red for validity, not leakage. Rename it (e.g. gbk). Also replace any_value(category_id) with min() to avoid the nondeterminism seen in C20.
critiques.kill_test: difference of differences: compare the gain on pairs whose user acquired in the category 1-2 days ago with the gain on 8+ days ago; no difference refutes the hazard mechanism.

critiques.text: Suspicion only; the card's own batch test is green. The final QUALIFY row_number() <= 60 orders by sum(h2.p2 / s.rk), a parallel floating-point aggregate. Near-ties at the cut can flip between runs. The twin, which has the same clause, is red on batch splits (2-3 keys answered in one run only), which shows the cut is unstable. Fix: order by round(sum(...), 9), then hash(user_id, cand).
critiques.kill_test: key level: rerun card and twin on the two halves after rounding the sort key. If the key mismatch disappears, it was float-order nondeterminism and not a batch leak; if it persists, look for a real cross-user path.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level and reads [t-14d, t); first_ts and peak come from the past window. However, the card is INVALID: the CTE alias 'fs' is forbidden, and the machine test is red for validity only. Rename fs (e.g. firsts).
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compute at t-24h; if days-since-peak and share-vs-peak keep the same gain, lifecycle phase is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: Machine test red: 302,446,050 rows on probe_day_1 (limit 150M). Up to 15 seeds per active user are joined to every b in pst with n >= 2, with no top-k per a. No time leak: lg uses views in (tb-72h, tb) with tb < t. Add a QUALIFY top-k per a (e.g. <= 20, ties by hash(a, b)).
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: once the row count fits, if the mu-shuffled twin gives the same gain, lag matching adds nothing beyond the pst counts.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level and reads [t-14d, t). percent_rank is ordered by first_ts, then product_id, so it is deterministic. Nothing depends on active_users.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: the twin (popularity-decile pseudo-siblings) has nearly the same nearest-column R2 (0.62/0.71). If it gives the same gain, brand-category siblings are not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. All reads are before t. active_users only selects uf. However, ucd reads 21 days, beyond the 14-day base. On anchors before 2020-01-22 that window is truncated at 2020-01-01, so the tenure values for early anchors are biased short. This is a shift risk, not a leak.
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compare the feature distribution for anchors 01-15..01-21 with later anchors. A level jump with no gain change means the tenure signal is a window artefact.

critiques.text: No leak found. The co-view graph comes from all sessions in [t-7d, t). ut is restricted to active users with per-user ranking, ties broken by product_id. The cnc and cn QUALIFY clauses break ties by hash. Batch test green. Side note: 6.05 s median.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the neighbour-shuffled twin (coverage 0.118 vs 0.178) gives the same gain per covered pair, reverse-neighbour recall is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found: carts and purchases are in [t-7d, t) for active users only. But f_x_c_opencart_hours_log has rho 0.999 and R2 1.0 with uc_last_cp_h, and f_x_c_opencart_items_log has R2 0.916 with uc_distinct_viewed_7d. It also rests on cart counts (cart level).
critiques.kill_test: key level: drop the opencart columns, keep uc_last_cp_h; if the gain is unchanged, the card is redundant.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level, hourly median prices in [t-14d, t). lag is ordered by h, and arg_max(dl, h) has a unique h per product. Deterministic.
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compute at t-24h; if price-change age and size keep their gain, recency of the change is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No time or batch leak found: product-level, and first-seen is capped at 336 h. However, the card is INVALID: the column alias 'fs' is forbidden, and the machine test is red for validity. Also, 'it' scans all of hist since 2020-01-01; restrict it to the products seen in [t-14d, t).
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the hash-ranked id twin gives the same gain, product_id order as a newness proxy is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level, prices in [t-9d, t), and the 'recent' split is [t-2d, t). Nothing depends on active_users. The twin splits days by hash.
critiques.kill_test: difference of differences: compare the gain in categories with drop share in the top decile against the rest. No difference refutes the price-wave mechanism (rival: f_x_dfs_c_cart_per_view_3d, R2 0.69).

critiques.text: No leak found. The graph comes from all sessions in [t-7d, t). The user's last 10 sessions are for active users in [t-14d, t), ordered by max(event_time), then user_session. The per-user share uses only the user's own sessions. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the session-shuffled twin (coverage 0.047) gives the same gain, cross-session convergence is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: Veto: the batch machine test is red for card and twin (up to 71,296 keys with different values in their half). Cause: nondeterminism from any_value(category_id) and any_value(brand) in acqb and in tp, under parallel scans, for products whose events carry several categories or brands. This changes the brand lift and the NOT EXISTS category filter. Replace them with min() or arg_max(x, event_time) with a key tiebreak.
critiques.kill_test: key level: rerun on the two halves after replacing any_value with min(). The batch test should go green and the loyalty-lift gain should stay; if the gain vanishes, it came from the nondeterministic mapping.

critiques.text: Suspicion only; product-level queries get no batch test. it uses any_value(category_id), which is the same nondeterminism that turned C20 red. A product with several categories can land in a different category or band per run, so band and cat rates are not reproducible. Use min(category_id). No time leak: reads [t-7d, t).
critiques.kill_test: staleness: run the query twice on the same anchor and also at t-24h. If products change band between the two same-day runs, the column is nondeterministic. If the gain remains with min(category_id), the price-band mechanism stands.

critiques.text: Suspicion only, no machine test red. any_value(category_id) and any_value(brand) in it can assign a multi-brand or multi-category product to a different sibling window per run, the same nondeterminism as C20. Use min(). No time leak: reads [t-7d, t).
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: the twin is already rho 0.85 with the card. If the hash-price twin gives the same gain after the min() fix, price-neighbour siblings are not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level, [t-7d, t); v1 is [t-1d, t). No active_users dependence. The twin's day choice uses hash(category_id).
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compute at t-24h; if the stalled-share gain is unchanged, it is only a stable category trait.

critiques.text: No leak found. Acquisitions and first touches are in [t-14d, t), and post-acquisition first touches are censored at t. The lifts are global, and active_users only selects us. Ties are broken by key. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: the twin is already rho 0.88 with the card. If the time-shuffled twin gives the same gain, the post-acquisition order adds nothing beyond co-acquisition (rival: cf_tr_lift_max, R2 0.61).

critiques.text: No leak found: active users' views in [t-14d, t), lag ordered by event_time. But f_x_c_cat_return_episodes_log has rho 0.986 and R2 0.972 with uc_active_days_14d, and the gap column has R2 0.788 with the same column.
critiques.kill_test: key level: drop the card and keep uc_active_days_14d; if the gain is unchanged, it is a duplicate.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level, hourly user counts in [t-14d, t). lag is ordered by h, and the arg_max key is unique per product. Deterministic.
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compute at t-24h; if hours-since-return keeps its gain, the 'comeback' timing is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No time or batch leak found: product-level, [t-14d, t), acquisitions in [t-7d, t). However, the card is INVALID: the CTE column alias 'fs' is forbidden, and the machine test is red for validity. Rename it. Note that 'newcomer' is defined by the window start, so it is window-censored on every anchor.
critiques.kill_test: difference of differences: compare the gain for target users first seen within 48h with older users; no difference refutes the newcomer-item mechanism.

critiques.text: Veto: the batch machine test is red for card and twin (5-9 keys answered in one run only). Clause: it = ... FROM w WHERE category_id IN (SELECT category_id FROM cats) GROUP BY product_id with max(category_id). cats comes from the active users' recent categories, so a multi-category product's assigned category, and therefore the top-40 per category, depends on which other users are in the batch. Compute it over all categories, then filter top by cats. Also 8.37 s median.
critiques.kill_test: key level: after computing 'it' over all categories, the batch test must go green. If the gain changes materially, part of it came from batch-dependent top sets.

critiques.text: No leak found. Active users' events in [t-48h, t). LEAD is over a user_session window ordered by event_time, then hash(product_id, event_type), so it is deterministic. The user totals uu are per user. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the within-day time-shuffled twin gives the same gain, dwell and bounce timing are not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. Active users' views in [t-48h, t); product price is arg_max(price, event_time) in [t-7d, t). Minor caveat: equal event_time with different prices makes arg_max tie-dependent; adding a key tiebreak is advised. Batch test green.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the neighbour-shuffled price twin gives the same gain, the user's price position within the consideration set is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. Other users' sessions in [t-7d, t) come from hist, not filtered by active_users, so they are batch-independent. The current session is the active user's own. Neighbour cuts are ordered by s_ts, then hash(user_session), and by sim, then hash. Batch test green. Cost note: 38.8 s median, under 60 s but above the 20 s target.
critiques.kill_test: twin as a factor: if the item-substituted twin (coverage 0.035) gives the same gain, session-kNN similarity is not the mechanism.

critiques.text: No leak found. Product-level, [t-14d, t), acquisitions in [t-7d, t). lag is ordered by s0/c0, then user_session. Minor: arg_min(category_id or user_session, event_time) can tie when a cart and a purchase share a timestamp; adding a key tiebreak is advised.
critiques.kill_test: staleness: compute at t-24h; if the return-visit and cold-category lifts keep their gain, they are stable item traits (rival: i_cat_multi_buy_14d, R2 0.763).
